newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta developer seeks tax break on hotel project.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta developer seeks tax break on hotel project.

text.p: A land developer asked City of Atlanta for a property tax exemption for a proposed $88 million hotel and residential complex on the perimeter of Centennial Olympic Park, Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported Thursday.
If the city grants enterprise zone status to the developer, Legacy Properties International, the firm would be exempt from property taxes for the first five years.

Legacy President David Martin said the five-acre high-rise project would create 450 new jobs. It would include a 322-room Doubletree Suites Hotel, a 50-unit condominium, a 140-unit residential development and a 125,000-square foot retail center.

Without the waiver, the developer would pay about $500,000 a year in property taxes for the first five years. City officials said the project could produce more than that amount via hotel taxes, business license fees and other charges.
Martin requested the exemption from the city council on Wednesday but the council postponed action.
